name: Last-mile / infill industrial
summary: Smaller (≈40k–250k SF) infill distribution and delivery-station buildings cost more per SF than bulk warehouses: fixed costs spread over less area, sites are often brownfield, and the ratio of paved van/trailer parking to building area is several times higher. No public source isolates "last-mile" product, so the default starts from Cushman & Wakefield's 2026 small-building model ($144 psf at 109,200 SF) and RLB metro ranges for the infill markets where this product concentrates.

typicalSize.method: C&W small model is 109,200 SF (e2); infill/last-mile product typically 40k–250k SF (judgment), mid 120k SF.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre at FAR ~0.20–0.37: delivery stations and IOS-heavy infill sites carry large van/trailer yards (FAR 0.20–0.30); conventional infill shallow-bay at ~0.35. Mid FAR 0.275 × 43,560 ≈ 12,000 SF/acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Car + delivery-van stalls per building SF: ~1–4 per 1,000 SF (delivery stations stage 1+ van per 1,000 SF plus employee cars); trailer stalls are a separate line.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Mid $150 = C&W 2026 small-building average $144 psf (e1) plus ~4% for the larger paved van/trailer yards typical of last-mile sites (bulk sitework already in C&W). Low $110 ≈ RLB low bounds in sunbelt infill markets (Dallas $75–$155 midpoint $115, Miami $80–$160 midpoint $120; e7/e8). High $220 ≈ RLB national median-of-highs ($228, e3) and the top of LA/Chicago ranges ($230–$245; e4/e6) — dense coastal infill with multi-story or heavy brownfield work can exceed this (NYC $155–$250, e5). RSMeans 2019 30k SF warehouse ($119–$131, e9) escalated to 2026 lands inside the range.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P, core & shell, spec office, on-site paving for cars/vans/trailers, on-site utilities and stormwater; excludes environmental remediation beyond typical, multi-story ramps, fleet EV charging, land, soft costs, off-sites and fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (110/150 = 0.73); premium ≈ high/mid (220/150 = 1.47) tempered to 1.3 for single-story product with heavy yard; luxury 1.6 for multi-story/ramped urban logistics (NYC/LA range tops e4/e5).

systemSplit.method: Warehouse-distribution split (C&W category shares, e10) shifted ~6 points from structure (03/05) into paving (32) and earthwork (31) to reflect the higher yard-to-building ratio; slightly more electrical/security (26/28) for fleet operations. Judgment — verify.

cost.method: Copied from _blocks/parking.json item parking-surface ($3,500/$6,500/$12,000 per space, 2025). Quantity ~1.5 stalls per 1,000 SF (vans + cars).
Same build-up as warehouse-distribution: 660 SF stall = 73 SY × heavy-duty concrete $85–$170/SY (paving block). ~1 stall per 10,000 SF.

lineItems.name: Fleet EV charging make-ready + Level 2 chargers (optional)

cost.method: Sum of _blocks/energy.json items ev-make-ready ($2,500/$4,000/$8,650 per port, 2022) and ev-l2-port ($6,000/$9,000/$16,000, 2021) — expressed in the older year (2022). Quantity 1 port per 2,000 SF (≈ one per 2 van stalls) — judgment; utility service upgrade not included.

lineItems.name: Dock door package (door, leveler, seal, bumpers, light)

cost.method: Same derived build-up as warehouse-distribution (door $4k–$7k + leveler $7k–$14k + seal/bumpers/light $1.5k–$4k). Last-mile buildings use fewer dock doors and more grade-level/van doors: ~1 per 10,000 SF.

pctOfHard.method: Bulk-warehouse soft-cost range (10–20%, see warehouse-distribution) plus ~1–2 points for infill entitlements, traffic studies, Phase I/II environmental and smaller project size. RSMeans architectural fee 7% (e9) is the upper bound for A/E.

softCosts.notes: Excludes financing, land and remediation beyond typical.

design.method: Slightly above bulk warehouse because infill sites are less standardised (judgment).

hard.method: Brownfield/infill unknowns (old foundations, contaminated soils, utility conflicts) → 4–10% (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $110 × 1.05; max ≈ NYC/LA RLB tops ($250) × 1.2 for soft costs. Multi-story urban logistics can exceed this and should be checked separately.

source.title: 2026 Americas Industrial Construction Cost Guide (landing page)

evidence.quote: Small projects averaged $144 psf (+3.6% YOY), medium $87 psf (+2.8% YOY), and large $78 psf (+2.3% YOY).
evidence.scopeNotes: Model 109,200-SF distribution building (size per CRE Daily); ground-up core and shell. Average of 46 Americas markets incl. Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, so not a pure US figure.

source.title: Industrial Construction Costs Rise Across Americas

evidence.quote: A 109,200-SF small project averaged $144 PSF in mid-2026 … A 476,400-SF medium project averaged $87 PSF … A 901,000-SF large project averaged $78 PSF
evidence.scopeNotes: Secondary report of the C&W 2026 guide; gives the model building sizes behind the small/medium/large averages.

evidence.scopeNotes: low/high here = median of the 18 U.S. city LOW values (140) and median of the HIGH values (227.5), computed by the researcher; un-weighted, coastal-heavy city sample, so above a true national average.

source.title: Warehouse Construction Cost Model (Brick Veneer / Reinforced Concrete)

evidence.quote: Subtotal $95.42/SF (open shop) … Contractor Fees (General Conditions, Overhead, Profit) 25% $23.85 … Architectural Fees 7% … Total $127.62 (open shop) / $139.76 (union)
evidence.scopeNotes: value = open-shop subtotal + 25% contractor fees ($95.42 + $23.85), architectural fee removed; high = union equivalent ($104.50 + $26.12). 30,000-SF, 24-ft brick-veneer warehouse; building only, sitework not shown. 2019 dollars.

source.title: Industrial Construction Costs Rise Across Americas

evidence.quote: Structural and enclosure work was the biggest cost category … about 34% of a small warehouse budget … about 37% for a large project. Architectural work represented about 22% of costs on small projects and roughly 15% on large projects.
evidence.scopeNotes: C&W 2026 cost-category shares (structure/enclosure 34-37%, architectural 15-22%; the article also puts MEP near 6-7% across sizes); the remaining ~35-45% is not itemised in the article (presumably sitework and GC/fees).

openQuestions: No public cost source isolates last-mile/delivery-station product; a public delivery-station budget (municipal incentive filing) would help.
